maria: heads up — after the runtime patch that updated kernel-ranking heuristics, we're seeing a 20-30% token throughput drop on the SM92 test fleet (cust-a100-sm92). looks like the selector is picking the fp8-tensorcore path, then falling back to slower kernel mid-stream for some sequences. :thinking:

maria: sample log from one request (truncated):
```
[2026-03-12T15:22:01Z] kernel_select: chosen=fp8_tc_v2 candidate_score=0.87
[2026-03-12T15:22:01Z] kernel_runtime: fallback_detected=true reason=unsupported_driver_fp8
[2026-03-12T15:22:01Z] exec: kernel=fp32_generic tokens/s=8500
[2026-03-12T15:22:01Z] expected_fp8_perf=12000 tokens/s
```

maria: repro command: `perf-bench --model gptx-6b --batch 8 --seqlen 512 --device cuda:0 --kernel-probe`

jin: do we know which driver/runtime combo flipped? fp8 TC kernels need both driver + cuBLAS/cuDNN bits. what are driver versions on the failing hosts? :mag_right:

maria: driver is 535.86, cudnn 9.1 on the fleet image. the canary (no issues) has 536.x + cudnn 9.2.

perf-bot: microbench summary (avg over 100 runs):
- host A (535.86): fp8 speculative path selected then fallback -> 8.5k toks/s
- host B (536.12): fp8 direct path -> 12.1k toks/s

perf-bot: annotation: fallback path incurs extra kernel relaunch + memcpy for format conversion (~1.4x overhead).

taylor: sounds like our capability probe is too optimistic. we currently probe SM via cuDeviceGetAttribute and then assume fp8 OK for sm>=92. but driver-level FP8 support can be gated by cuBLAS/cuDNN presence and nvml reported compute capability flags. we should: 
1) add an explicit runtime-capability bit (RUNTIME_SUPPORT_FP8) that requires a successful small fp8 microkernel run (no fallback) at startup
2) avoid speculative fp8 picks for sequences > 1024 until the runtime probe is validated

matt: also worth noting: KV-cache reuse changes effective sequence-length distribution. when prefix reuse causes bursts of long effective seqlen, the selector may flip kernel mid-request because prefix vs generation path differ. we should make kernel selection aware of per-request effective seqlen (prefix + gen) and pin kernel for whole request.

maria: good point. currently selection happens per-chunk. i'll sketch a patch to evaluate selection at request start and only allow mid-request change for explicit fallback (hard failure), not performance mismatch.

jin: quick checklist for the fix: 
- runtime probe: run tiny fp8 matmul microkernel, confirm result parity threshold and no fallback path triggered
- driver check: parse `nvidia-smi --query` for driver version and cudnn presence, but consider this advisory only
- kernel selector: add config `speculative_fp8=true/false` and default false for dedicated fleets with driver < 536
- pin kernel per-request to avoid KV-cache seqlen thrash

ops-bot: deployment suggestion: revert the kernel-ranking heuristics for stable fleet, issue hotfix to capability probe, then roll out speculative_fp8=false to 10% canaries for 24h. if green, promote. otherwise auto-revert. :gear:

maria: I'll open a small PR with the probe + selector gating. adding tests: fp8 microkernel smoke, runtime probe failure simulation, and a seqlen-pin e2e. target deploy to canary fleet tomorrow morning.

matt: thanks — also add a perf regression alert to the rollout job so we auto-surface token/s drops >10% within 1h.

taylor: we should also log a capability bit in the console so customers see why fp8 wasn't used (driver vs cudnn vs probe). helps support triage. :+1:

maria: ack, will include capability flags and short explanation string. will tag you all on the PR. :pray:
